speaker: Attorney
text: I want to shift gears a little and go over some follow-up topics. First, the written statement you mentioned earlier. When did you give that statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few days after. I think it was the Tuesday or the Wednesday. A deputy called me and asked if I'd come by and write down what I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you go to the sheriff's office, or did the deputy come to you?

speaker: Witness B
text: I went there. To the substation. My sister drove me.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did your sister go in with you?

speaker: Witness B
text: She came in and sat in the lobby. She didn't come in the room.

speaker: Attorney
text: Who was in the room with you when you wrote it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just the deputy. He gave me a form and a pen and said take my time.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was it the same deputy you talked to at the scene that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. The one at the scene was older. This one was younger. I could be wrong, there were a lot of them out there that day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Did the deputy ask you questions before you started writing?

speaker: Witness B
text: He asked me to just write it in my own words. Then after, he read it and asked me a couple of things.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember what he asked?

speaker: Witness B
text: He asked what time it was, about. And he asked if I'd ever met anybody involved. I said no.

speaker: Attorney
text: Had you?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't know anybody. I was just there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did he ask you to add anything to the statement after he read it?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. He said it was fine. I signed it and dated it.

speaker: Attorney
text: How long was the statement, roughly?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not long. Maybe a page. Most of a page. My handwriting's big.

speaker: Attorney
text: You reviewed that statement before today, correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. You all sent me a copy and I read it last week.

speaker: Attorney
text: And when you read it last week, was there anything in it you thought was wrong?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It's what I wrote. It's what happened.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything you'd change about it today?

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe I'd write more. I was nervous. But I wouldn't change anything that's in there.

speaker: Attorney
text: In that statement, you wrote, quote, "I saw the whole thing," end quote. Do you remember writing that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: What did you mean by that?

speaker: Witness B
text: I meant I saw it. The car coming, the truck turning, and then when it happened. I saw the whole thing.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: I did answer. That's what I meant.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone suggest that phrase to you, "I saw the whole thing"?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Those are my words.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the deputy tell you what to write in any way?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. He didn't tell me anything except to take my time and write what I saw.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you use any notes when you wrote the statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't have any notes. I didn't write anything down that day. I was too shook up.

speaker: Attorney
text: Between the afternoon of the collision and the day you wrote the statement, did you talk with anybody about what you'd seen?

speaker: Witness B
text: My sister, mostly. She picked me up right after, so she was the first one I really talked to.

speaker: Attorney
text: What did you tell her?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just that I saw a wreck. That a car went under a truck and kept going. I was crying, honestly. I wasn't real detailed.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did she ask you questions about it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some. She asked was I okay. She asked did I need to go to the doctor. I said no, I just wanted to go home.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you talk with anyone else before you wrote the statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: My husband, that night. And my daughter called me the next day because my sister told her.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any of them tell you anything about the collision that they had heard from somewhere else?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: My daughter said it was on the news. I told her I didn't want to hear about it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did she tell you what was on the news?

speaker: Witness B
text: She started to and I stopped her. I said I was there, I don't need to hear it from the TV.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you watch any news coverage of the collision at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I turned it off when it came on. I didn't want to see it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you read anything about it, in the paper or online?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. People would send me things and I wouldn't open them.

speaker: Attorney
text: Who sent you things?

speaker: Witness B
text: Just people I know. Somebody from church. A cousin. I'd see the picture and I'd just close it.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you may have seen a picture?

speaker: Witness B
text: Like a little picture on my phone, a thumbnail. I didn't look at it. I didn't read it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember what that picture showed?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I closed it. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just didn't look.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Have you ever looked at any photographs of the scene taken by anyone else?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not until you all, I guess, if there's some today. I haven't seen any.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you looked at any maps or diagrams of the intersection since the collision?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you gone back to that intersection since?

speaker: Witness B
text: I've driven through it. I have to. It's the way to my sister's. But I haven't stopped at the store since.

speaker: Attorney
text: You haven't been back to the store at all?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I just don't want to.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you drive through the intersection now, do you look at it?

speaker: Witness B
text: I try not to. I just go.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you talked with anyone who was at the scene that day, other than the people you've mentioned?

speaker: Witness B
text: The lady from the store. The one who came out. I talked to her that afternoon.

speaker: Attorney
text: After that afternoon, have you talked with her again?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I haven't seen her since.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you talked with anyone from either side of this case, other than the attorneys, before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: An investigator called me once. I think he was from your side. I told him basically what I told the deputy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you give that investigator a written or recorded statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a phone call. Maybe ten minutes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone from the trucking company or its insurer contact you?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I know of. I got a letter about today. That's it.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: For the record, that letter was the notice of deposition.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Ma'am, did anyone, at any time, tell you what to say today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you meet with anyone to prepare for today?

speaker: Witness B
text: I talked to your office on the phone to set up the time. And they told me to just tell the truth and say if I don't know something.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone go over the substance of your testimony with you?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. They just said read your statement if you want to. So I did.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Let me ask you some questions about your eyesight. Do you wear glasses?

speaker: Witness B
text: Reading glasses. Only for reading. For close up.

speaker: Attorney
text: How long have you worn reading glasses?

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe six or seven years. Since my forties.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you need glasses or contacts for distance?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. My distance is fine. I drive without glasses. My license doesn't have any restriction.

speaker: Attorney
text: When was your last eye exam?

speaker: Witness B
text: Last year, I think. Maybe a little more. They said my distance was good and gave me a new reading prescription.

speaker: Attorney
text: And before the collision, when was your last exam?

speaker: Witness B
text: The one before that was maybe two years before. Same thing. Distance was fine.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you ever been told you have any problem with your eyes, other than needing reading glasses?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any trouble with glare, or seeing in bright light?

speaker: Witness B
text: No more than anybody. If it's real bright I squint like anybody.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing your reading glasses that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. They were in my purse. I'd used them in the store to read a label and then I put them away.

speaker: Attorney
text: So at the time of the collision, your reading glasses were in your purse.

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you weren't wearing sunglasses.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I don't think I even had them with me. I'd left them in my sister's car the week before.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing a hat or anything over your eyes?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. No hat.

speaker: Attorney
text: How tall are you?

speaker: Witness B
text: Five foot six.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you wearing any kind of heels or anything that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Flat sandals. I don't wear heels. My feet won't let me.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you were standing at about your normal height.

speaker: Witness B
text: Five six. Same as now.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you standing the whole time, or were you sitting at some point?

speaker: Witness B
text: Standing. I'd been inside a while shopping and then I went out to wait, and I was standing.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: At the moment the car reached the intersection, were you standing or sitting?

speaker: Witness B
text: Standing.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you on any kind of step, or curb, or raised area?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. It was just the ground out front. Maybe the concrete in front of the store, I don't remember a step.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Now I want to ask about what, if anything, was between you and the highway. When you were standing outside, out front of the store, what objects were around you?

speaker: Witness B
text: There was a couple of signs. Like the store signs, a sign by the road. And there was a bench shelter thing out front. A little covered bench. And the gas, or the ice box, I think there was an ice box by the door.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's take those one at a time. The signs. What kind of signs?

speaker: Witness B
text: One was the store sign, up on a pole, a tall one. And there were some little signs, like the kind that stick in the ground, advertising stuff. Bait, I think, and something about a sale.

speaker: Attorney
text: How big were the small signs?

speaker: Witness B
text: Small. Like yard signs. Down low, knee high maybe.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the tall sign on the pole. Where was the sign itself, up high or down low?

speaker: Witness B
text: Up high. Way up. You'd have to look up to see it.

speaker: Attorney
text: The bench shelter you mentioned. Can you describe it?

speaker: Witness B
text: It's a little roof over a bench. Like a bus stop kind of thing, but I don't think a bus stops there. Posts on the corners, a roof. Open on the sides mostly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was it enclosed in any way?

speaker: Witness B
text: There was a back on it, I think. Part of a back. But you could see through the sides.

speaker: Attorney
text: What was it made of, if you know?

speaker: Witness B
text: Metal posts, I think. A metal roof. I didn't really pay attention to it.

speaker: Attorney
text: How tall was it, approximately?

speaker: Witness B
text: Taller than me. Maybe seven feet. I don't know exactly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was anybody sitting on the bench?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember. I don't think so.

speaker: Attorney
text: Anything else between you and the highway? Any vehicles parked in front of the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: There might have been a car or two parked. I'm not sure. There wasn't anything big. No trucks parked out there that I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any trees or bushes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not really out front. There's some trees further off, toward the back and along the side. Not in front.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any fences?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not right there. There were fences further down, the ones the car went through. Those are down the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: So summarizing, between you and the highway there were a couple of signs, the bench shelter, and possibly a parked car or two?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Mischaracterizes.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll rephrase. In your own words, what was between you and the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: A couple of signs, a bench shelter thing, nothing big. That's what I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any of those things block your view of the highway?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Like I said, nothing was in the way.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask about the sun. Do you remember where the sun was that afternoon?

speaker: Witness B
text: It was up. Still pretty high. It was a sunny day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was it in front of you, behind you, to the side?

speaker: Witness B
text: It wasn't in my eyes. I remember it was hot on my arms, but it wasn't in my eyes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you have to shade your eyes at any point?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I don't remember doing that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you squinting?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It wasn't like that. It wasn't in my face.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Asked and answered.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were there any shadows or anything like that, that made it hard to see the road?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was just a bright clear day. You could see everything.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there any haze, dust, smoke, anything in the air?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. It was clear. It hadn't rained.

speaker: Attorney
text: Now, you told us earlier you were waiting for your sister. At the time of the collision, where was your attention, if you remember?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: On the road. I was looking for her car. She comes from the west, so I was looking that way, up the road toward the hill.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. I want to come back to your written statement for a moment. Besides "I saw the whole thing," do you recall what else you wrote?

speaker: Witness B
text: I wrote that the car came down the hill fast, that the truck was turning, and that the car went under it and kept going and hit a pole. And then I wrote the truck stopped down the side road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you write anything about where you were?

speaker: Witness B
text: I wrote I was outside the store waiting on my sister. Out front.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you write anything more specific than that?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just out front of the store. That's all he asked.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the deputy draw anything, or ask you to draw anything?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. No drawing. Just writing.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the deputy show you any map or photo?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you write how fast you thought the car was going?

speaker: Witness B
text: I wrote fast. I think I wrote "real fast." I didn't put a number.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you put a number anywhere in the statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe the time. I put around four thirty. That's the only number, I think, besides the date.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything that you remember now, sitting here today, that you didn't put in that statement?

speaker: Witness B
text: Little things. Like the store lady coming out. Calling my sister. I didn't put all that. I just put the wreck.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is there anything you remember now that's different from what you wrote?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing different. Just more.

speaker: Attorney
text: Has your memory of that afternoon changed over time, in your view?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: No. If anything I remember it too well. I still think about it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you have any difficulty with your memory generally?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I keep track of all my clients' medications. I'd lose my job if I forgot things.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me ask about the period after the statement. Have you discussed the collision with anyone in the time since you wrote it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not much. It comes up sometimes with my family. I don't like to talk about it.

speaker: Attorney
text: When it comes up with your family, does anyone tell you things they've heard about it?

speaker: Witness B
text: They know not to. I asked them not to.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you ever posted anything about it online?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Never. I don't do that.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone ever offer you anything in connection with your testimony? Money, anything at all?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nothing. I'm not getting anything. I took off work to be here.

speaker: Attorney
text: I appreciate that. Do you have any relationship with the store, other than being a customer?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I just shop there sometimes. Used to.

speaker: Attorney
text: Any relationship with any trucking company?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. My brother-in-law drives for a moving company, but that's nothing to do with this.

speaker: Attorney
text: Does your brother-in-law work for the company that's the defendant in this case?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Not as far as I know. It's a different company. Little local outfit.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you ever been involved in a lawsuit yourself?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. Let me go back to one more thing on eyesight. At the distance of the highway from the front of the store, could you read, for example, a license plate?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Witness B
text: I didn't try to read any license plate. I could see the cars fine. I could see colors and shapes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you tell the color of the car?

speaker: Witness B
text: Dark. Black or real dark blue. Dark.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you tell the color of the trailer?

speaker: Witness B
text: White. All white. Big and white.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Ma'am, would you like a short break, or are you okay to keep going?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'm okay. Let's keep going. I'd rather just get it done.

speaker: Attorney
text: Some water there if you need it.

speaker: Witness B
text: Thank you.

speaker: Attorney
text: Between the collision and five o'clock, did you stay outside the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I stayed out front. I didn't go anywhere. The store lady came out and stood with me for a while.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you ever go inside during that time?

speaker: Witness B
text: Maybe for a minute, to get some water. She brought me inside for a minute and then I went back out because I was waiting for my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. I think that covers that area. Thank you, ma'am.

speaker: Witness B
text: You're welcome.
